new_statements.quote: 3. Der Akzent. Als Regel gilt: den Ton hat die vorletzte Silbe. Wörter, die als Proparoxytona zu sprechen sind (wie die Perfekta auf -ile der zwei- oder mehrsilbigen Stämme und einiger anderer), sind durch den Akzent als solche gekennzeichnet.
new_statements.translation: 3. The accent. The rule is: the stress falls on the penultimate syllable. Words that are to be pronounced as proparoxytones (such as the perfects in -ile of di- or polysyllabic stems, and a few others) are marked as such by the accent sign.
new_statements.citation: Spiss, Cassian. 1904. Kingoni und Kisutu. Mitteilungen des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen VII, III. Abt. (Afrikanische Studien): 270-414. [Grammar of 'Kingoni' = Old (Nguni-type) Tanzanian Ngoni; Kisutu only in the vocabulary]
new_statements.locator: p. 273, §I 'Das Alphabet und die Aussprache', item 3 'Der Akzent' (PDF page 862 of the saved volume scan; page 4 of)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK: Opened (page 4 = printed p. 273 = PDF page 862 of) and the rendered image. Under the heading "I. Das Alphabet und die Aussprache", item "3. Der Akzent." reads exactly: "Als Regel gilt: den Ton hat die vorletzte Silbe. Wörter, die als Proparoxytona zu sprechen sind (wie die Perfekta auf -ile der zwei- oder mehrsilbigen Stämme und einiger anderer), sind durch den Akzent als solche gekennzeichnet." Verbatim match with the reader's quote (the extracted text layer misreads "-ile" as "-He"; the page image shows -ile). Also confirmed on the same page, §1: "nur e klingt, besonders wenn der Ton darauf ruht, wie ä", and on printed p. 284 (PDF page 873), demonstrative section: "Die größer…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the penultimate syllable by rule; a closed morphological set (perfect forms in -ile built on stems of two or more syllables, plus a few other words) is antepenultimate and is flagged with a written accent in the grammar and vocabulary.
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenultimate accent in -ile perfects of di-/polysyllabic stems 'and some others' (marked in the text). In the demonstrative-pronoun section Spiss adds that greater or lesser distance is expressed by stronger or weaker stress on the first syllable of the demonstrative. §1 notes that e sounds like ä especially when it bears the accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms in a missionary grammar written 1898-1904 at Peramiho; no phrase-level statement. 'Ton' here means word accent, not lexical tone. IDENTITY: the described variety is the Zulu-derived speech of the Ngoni ruling stratum (Spiss pp. 270-271 calls it 'die unverfälschte Sprache der Zulukaffern'), which Glottolog assigns to Zulu [zul] = zulu1248, not to tanz1241; modern Tanzanian Ngoni (tanz1241, N12, Ngonyani 2003 'Chingoni') is the Kisutu-descended substrate language, for which Spiss gives only vocabulary and no accent statement.
new_statements.identity_note: The one open, first-hand accent statement (Spiss 1904, p. 273) describes 'Kingoni' as spoken by the Ngoni ruling stratum at Songea in 1898-1904, which Spiss himself identifies as Zulu (pp. 270-271) and which Glottolog's record for the work (ref 8093) codes as 'Old Tanzanian Ngoni = Zulu [zul]' (zulu1248; Nguni S42), with Kisutu (the substrate) 'dominated demographically of Ndendeule (Moser 1983:36)'. Modern Tanzanian Ngoni tanz1241 (N12; Ngonyani 2003 'Chingoni') is the descendant of that Kisutu/Sutu substrate after the Nguni language was lost (Ngonyani 2001; Wikipedia). Doke 1945:54, quoted in the Glottolog record, states that Spiss's grammar 'deals only with Ngoni', and the Kisutu material is confined to the vocabulary, which carries no accent statement. The quoted rule is therefore a first-hand statement for the extinct Nguni-type Ngoni of Tanzania, not for tanz1241; it could be catalogued under zulu1248 (Nguni Ngoni) with a dialect label, but not under tanz1241.

Also p. 273 §1: e sounds like ä especially when accented; in the demonstrative section, nearer/further distance is signalled by stronger/weaker stress on the first syllable.
